name: Downtown and the Cultural District
tagline: Bernard Avenue, the beach and the waterfront park
description: Kelowna's centre running down Bernard Avenue to the lake, with the restaurants, breweries and the cultural district of galleries and theatres, ending at City Park and its beach. It is the only genuinely walkable part of the city and where the summer evening life concentrates.
bestFor: Anyone who wants the lake, the restaurants and the galleries on foot
pros: City Park beach and the waterfront boardwalk
cons: The highest rents in the city
Very busy through July and August

name: Pandosy Village
tagline: The lakeside neighbourhood south of downtown
description: A walkable strip along Pandosy Street a few kilometres south of the centre, with independent shops, cafes and restaurants, backing onto Gyro Beach and the hospital. It has more neighbourhood character than downtown and sits between the lake and the residential Mission district behind.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting a walkable neighbourhood with a beach
pros: Gyro Beach and the lakeshore at the door
Independent shops and cafes rather than chains
cons: Ten minutes by car or bike to the centre

name: Glenmore and the North End
tagline: Residential valleys behind the city, with the rail trail
description: The residential districts running north from downtown up the Glenmore valley, with family housing, schools, Knox Mountain Park and the Okanagan Rail Trail passing through. Rents are below the lakeside districts and the cycle route into the centre takes about fifteen minutes.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting a lower rent with a cycle route into town
pros: Knox Mountain and the rail trail for running and cycling

name: West Kelowna
tagline: Across the bridge, wineries and lower rents
description: The separate municipality across the lake bridge, with a string of wineries on the western slopes, its own shopping and rents meaningfully below Kelowna proper. The bridge is the constraint: it is the only crossing and it backs up at peak times, which residents plan around and visitors do not expect.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting lower rents and the wineries on the doorstep
pros: Cheaper than Kelowna for equivalent housing
Wineries on the western slopes within minutes
Lake access and beaches on this side too
cons: The single bridge is a genuine daily bottleneck
Twenty to thirty minutes into downtown at peak

name: Lake Country and Big White Road
tagline: North to the vineyards, east to the ski hill
description: The area north along the lake through Lake Country's vineyards and orchards, and the road east climbing to Big White ski resort at 1,750m. Both are the country rather than the city: quieter, cheaper and requiring a car, with Kalamalka Lake north among the most striking in the province.
bestFor: Stays organised around the wineries or the ski hill rather than the city
pros: Big White and its ski terrain up the road
Cheaper and much quieter than the city
cons: Twenty-five to forty minutes from Kelowna
A car is essential and winter roads are demanding
